answer.reason: Several verses tell of Aroer beyond boundary mentions: Gad built it, and Joab's officers camped there when they numbered Israel.

clauses.english: was built by the children of Gad
clauses.quote: the children of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer

clauses.english: was where Joab and the captains camped when sent to number Israel
clauses.quote: they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer

doubts: ISA 17:2 (cities of Aroer forsaken) sits in a prophecy against Damascus and may concern another Aroer, so it was left out.

Many verses (DEU 2:36, DEU 3:12, DEU 4:48, JOS 12:2, JOS 13:9, JOS 13:16, 2KI 10:33) only use Aroer as a boundary marker; JDG 11:26 and 1CH 5:8 only say people dwelt there; JER 48:19 only addresses its inhabitant; none of these were used.
